name: צִדְקִיָּהוּ
gloss: Yahweh is righteousness; righteousness of Yah
summary: Chiefly the last king of Judah, Josiah's son Mattaniah, whom Nebuchadnezzar made king in place of Jehoiachin and renamed צִדְקִיָּהוּ (2Ki 24:17). He did evil in Yahweh's eyes, did not humble himself before Jeremiah, and rebelled against the king of Babylon though he had sworn by God; Jerusalem was taken, his sons slaughtered before his eyes, and he was blinded and taken to Babylon (2Ki 24:19–20; 25:7; 2Ch 36:12–13; Jer 39:6–7). Others bearing it: Zedekiah son of Kenaanah, who made iron horns and struck Micaiah (1Ki 22:11, 24); a lying prophet in Babylon (Jer 29:21); a prince in Jehoiakim's day (Jer 36:12); a son of Jeconiah (1Ch 3:16); and a sealer of Nehemiah's covenant (Neh 10:2). The name is צֶדֶק “righteousness” with the ‑i of joining and יָהוּ, the short form of Yahweh's name: “Yahweh is righteousness” or “righteousness of Yah”. In Zedekiah's reign Jeremiah gives the promise of the branch whose name is יַהְוֶה צִדְקֵנוּ, “Yahweh our righteousness” (Jer 23:5–6), the same two words in the other order.

evidence.note: “The king of Babylon made Mattaniah his uncle king in his place, and changed his name to צִדְקִיָּהוּ.”
The sons of Josiah: “the third, צִדְקִיָּהוּ”.
He did evil in Yahweh's eyes, and rebelled against the king of Babylon.
He did not humble himself before Jeremiah, and rebelled against Nebuchadnezzar, “who had made him swear by God”.
King Zedekiah sends to Jeremiah; the answer is that Yahweh will give him into Nebuchadnezzar's hand (Jer 21:7).
“Is there a word from Yahweh?” “There is: into the hand of the king of Babylon you will be given.”
His sons slaughtered at Riblah before his eyes; his eyes put out; bound and taken to Babylon. Also 2Ki 25:7.
“This is his name by which he will be called: יַהְוֶה צִדְקֵנוּ”: the elements of צִדְקִיָּהוּ, Yahweh's name and צֶדֶק.
“צִדְקִיָּה son of Kenaanah made himself horns of iron.”
Ahab son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah son of Maaseiah, “prophesying to you in my name falsely”.
Zedekiah son of Hananiah among the princes.
“The sons of Jehoiakim: Jeconiah his son, צִדְקִיָּה his son.”
On the sealed covenant: Nehemiah the Tirshatha “and צִדְקִיָּה”.

note: Two spellings: צִדְקִיָּהוּ and צִדְקִיָּה (1Ki 22:11; Neh 10:2; 1Ch 3:16), both under BDB r.ar.ag. Verse ranges in Jer 23 are cited as showing the two names share their elements; that the prophecy was framed against the king's name is not stated in the text and is not claimed. Neh 10:2 is TIPNR's Neh.10.1 (English numbering).
